To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
thiophosphate anions cleave the carbon-nitrogen bond of N-acylethyleneimine molecules and that the reaction products can be obtained in the form of stable neutral salts.
thiophosphate ions are capable of cleaving the C—N bond of N-acylethyleneimine derivatives and that the products of this reaction can be obtained in high yields by the use of a simple method.

N-acyl and N-phosphonyl ethyleneimines can be converted into N-acyl or N-phosphonylmethanephosphonic acid monoesters and S-[N-alkyl(aryl)phosphonyl]-β-mercaptooethylamine by reaction with thiophosphate anions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis of N-acylethylenimines, their reactions with thiophosphates, and the preparation of S-[N-acylethyleneamino]ethylthiophosphorothioic acid derivatives.
a new method for the preparation and cleavage of N-alkyl- and N-acylethyleneimine thiophosphate salts and the synthesis of S-[N-(alkyl, aryl)-β-aminoethoxy]thiophosphate salts.
the preparation, isolation, and properties of N-acylethyleneimine thiophosphates.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the cleavage of acylated ethyleneimines by monolithiothiphosphate is a convenient method to prepare N-acylated-β-mercaptolamines.
the reaction between N-acylethyl- and N-phos-phorylethyleneamines and thiophosphate anions proceeds with the formation of S-[N-acyl (phosphor-yl)-β-aminoethy1]thiophosphate ions.

the cleavage of the C=N bond of N-acylethyleneimine by the monolithiophosphate ion proceeds in two stages: (1) nucleophilic addition of the sulfur atom to the imine carbon atom, (2) elimination of a proton from the nitrogen atom of the resulting thiophosphonium ion with the formation of a thiophosphate ion.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
N-acyl and N-phosphorylethyleneimine derivatives can be cleaved by the monolithiotiophosphoric acid to give the corresponding S-[N- acyl or N-phosphorylaminoethyl]thio-phosphates.

the cleavage of the N-C bond in N-acyl and N-phosphorylethyleneimine by the monolithiophosphate ion proceeds via a nucleophilic substitution with the formation of a thiophosphoryl group in the α-position to the amino group.

the reaction of the N-acyl or N-phosphorylenimine with thiophosphates proceeds in the presence of a base, and the reaction of the imine with thiophosphate in the acid medium proceeds in a manner similar to the reaction with phosphorus oxychloride.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the cleavage of ethyleneimines by phosphorothioic acids is an important step in the synthesis of N-alkylphosphorothioates and that the cleavage products of ethyleneimine by phosphorothiolates can be used as intermediates in the synthesis of phosphoramidates.
the reaction of the monolithio-thiophosphate anions with the N-acylethyl-imine is a convenient method to prepare N-acyl and N-phospho-ryl β-mercatoethylamines.

the reaction of N-acyleneimines with the thiophosphate ion leads to the formation of the thiophosphate salt of the S-[N-α-acyl-β-aminoethylthiophosphoryl]acetic acid, which is unstable in the neutral form and decomposes with the elimination of acetic acid.
